candidate_reports.remark: DEBRIS-IN-ROAD (TREES & WIRES) TREES ACROSS THE ROAD. HORNE TOWN RD & MINERAL SPRINGS CHURCH RD.
Tree and Powerlines on Helms Road In Peachland.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. A brief_ but strong_ short-track tornado occurred on the northeast side of Candor in between Brutonville Road and I-73. Drone images and video provided by Eagle Springs Fire Chief assisted in determining the start point between Cherry Circle and Hurricane Drive where a significant number of uprooted and snapped trees occurred. The tornado quickly continued to track roughly northeast where significant damage occurred to a community center which had 3 of its exterior walls collapsed and several more softwood trees were snapped; consistent with high-end EF-1 to low-end EF-2 damage. The tornado continued across a small pond and snapped about 10 hardwood/softwood trees and removed a large portion of roof covering from a residence near Etta Drive. From this point_ the tornado quickly lifted_ not before snapping small branches_ before reaching I-73 with no visible damage from drone footage to the northeast.
Emergency manager reports one building destroyed and another severely damaged along with several large trees snapped in the Hurricane Drive and Hillview street areas.

Multiple trees down in this vicinity of Skibo Road and Morganton Road. Suspected beginning of tornado track based on initial reports.

The start of the Bonnie Doone tornado path based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 115 mph (EF-2) occurred on a short quarter-mile section between the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road while otherwise producing EF-0 to EF-1 damage along a discontinuous path for nearly 5.5 miles.
Several reports of storm damage including 18 wheeler flipped_ cars lifted and dropped_ roof damage_ power outages and trees down around the Walmart and Sams Club along Skibo Road.

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed just south of Beaver Creek Rd_ causing EF-1 damage as it crossed the road and moved northeastward. It eventually crossed a small section of the lake before lifting on the northern shoreline. Total path length: 1.07 miles Peak width: 50 yards Time on ground: 1 minute.
Numerous mature hardwood and pine trees downed_ snapped and twisted on Beaver Creek Road_ just south of Pea Ridge Road. Damage was coincident with a radar TDS.
SEVERAL TREES ARE DOWN along Beaver Creek Rd_ BOTH LANES OF TRAVEL ARE BLOCKED.

The start of the Linden_ NC tornado based on NWS storm survey. Maximum winds of 105 mph (EF-1) occurred along Hungry Creek Drive where several windows were blown out of a residence. The tornado tracked along a nearly continuous path for almost 1.25 miles.

A short lived EF-1 tornado developed near the West Regional Library and traveled northeastward. Several trees were snapped in the library parking lot and in the adjacent neighborhood to the north. No structural damage was apparent during the survey_ suggesting the strongest winds remained at treetop level.

Approximate beginning of tornado path. The tornado occurred along a 3.2 mile-long discontinuous path_ as it momentarily touched down and lifted several times before finally dissipating at the end of the indicated path. Damage consisted mainly of snapped and uprooted trees_ large tree branches broken off_ minor shingle and roof damage to several homes or structures_ many fences blown over_ and several power poles that were snapped and downed. There was also damage to patio furniture and signage at a service station at the intersection of Hwy 36 and Hwy 70 in Clayton. The max wind speed was 85 mph which is an EF-0 on the Enhanced Fujita Scale (EF Scale).
